summary:
Katsina stands under Nigeria's national framework and additionally operates its own Sharia criminal layer. Katsina is among the northern states that adopted Sharia criminal codes from 1999 onward, and the provisions cited remain in force.

Katsina's own statute is the Sharia Penal Code Law 2001, Law No. 2 of 2001, which came into operation on 20 June 2001 and was gazetted in Katsina State Gazette Vol. 12 No. 23 on 27 August 2001.

The code's sodomy provision reads: "Whoever commits the offence of sodomy shall be punished with stoning to death (rajm)". Katsina is one of three states, with Kaduna and Kebbi, whose sodomy text carries that wording.

Katsina's lesbianism provision is among the harshest in the northern block. Only Kano and Katsina reach stoning to death as the maximum for the lesbianism offence, against the harmonised code's base penalty of 50 lashes and up to six months. Katsina is one of only two states whose law carries death as the maximum for same-sex acts between women as well as men.

For a trans person held in Katsina, the penalty structure runs from lashing or caning to capital punishment. Lesbianism, defined as carnal acts or stimulation between women, is punishable by imprisonment or caning in most northern states, with death penalties applied in Kano and Katsina.

The Sharia layer in Katsina reaches women as well as men. Arrest data for these offences is limited, so the recorded enforcement picture is incomplete.

Presentation is separately exposed. Sources describe a cross-dressing layer in the northern states under which men who dress or behave as women face prison or a fine.
tangentialFactors:
Katsina's Sharia code belongs to a twelve-state northern block adopted in a wave that began with Zamfara's Shari'a Establishment Law, promulgated on 27 October 1999 and in force from 27 January 2000.

Enforcement of the cross-dressing layer is documented in a neighbouring northern state: a Kano court sentenced a TikTok user to one year in prison on 20 June 2025 over a cross-dressing video.

Residents of Katsina live under the Sharia Penal Code Law 2001 in addition to national law. The code's sodomy and lesbianism provisions carry the maximum penalties described, and its reach extends to women as well as men.

Arrest data for the Sharia offences is limited, so residents have little public record of how often the provisions are enforced.

Dress and behaviour are separately regulated: men who dress or behave as women face prison or a fine under the cross-dressing layer described for the northern states.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Katsina-specific prison housing rule, segregation policy or women's-wing measure for transgender prisoners appears in the sources. Placement of a trans prisoner in Katsina is not documented.

A global overview of LGBTQ people in prison contains no Nigeria entry, so no Katsina-specific trans-prisoner housing policy, special unit or segregation practice is recorded there.

Whether the cross-dressing provision is codified in Katsina's own Sharia Penal Code or applied through other provisions is not sourced.

No record of a death sentence being carried out for either offence in Katsina is present in the sources.
